core_obligations: Observe that the horizontal maps are monomorphisms by construction, so that the cartesian property reduces to a condition on morphisms from schemes (proof lines 8061-8062).
Reduce that condition to: g : U -> X' defines a point of X'_{/T} if and only if f o g defines a point of X_{/T} (proof lines 8062-8064).
Rewrite both sides as the containments g(U) in T' and (f o g)(U) in T of the reduced spaces (proof lines 8065-8067).
Use that T' was defined as |f_red|^{-1}(T) to conclude the equivalence (proof lines 8068-8069).
proof_roadmap: Pointwise criterion on scheme-valued g (proof lines 8062-8064).
Identification with the inverse-image definition of T' (proof lines 8065-8069).
difficulty_reason: For a morphism f : X' -> X of formal algebraic spaces over S, a closed subset T of the reduced space of X and T' its inverse image in the reduced space of X', the lemma asserts that the square with the recompletions X'_{/T'} and X_{/T} over X' and X is cartesian (statement lines 8045-8058). The proof is displayed in full: the horizontal arrows are seen to be monomorphisms by construction, which reduces the cartesian property to a pointwise condition on scheme-valued morphisms g : U -> X' (proof lines 8060-8064), and that condition is then read off from the definition of T' as the inverse image of T (proof lines 8065-8069). The level is H2 because the reduction step (monomorphism, hence it suffices to test on points) is the real content, while the final identification is immediate from the choice of T'.
